module_title: Types of Mountains, Highest Peaks, and the Ring of Fire
introduction: At this level, we will analyze the scientific classification of mountains based on their geological formation. We will also map the extreme points (highest peaks) of each continent and differentiate between critical geographical chokepoints: Straits and Isthmuses.

core_concepts.title: Types of Mountains
core_concepts.description: 1. Fold Mountains: Formed when tectonic plates collide, causing the Earth's crust to fold (e.g., Himalayas in Asia, Alps in Europe, Andes in South America). 2. Block Mountains: Formed when massive faulting causes large blocks of land to be displaced vertically (e.g., Black Forest in Germany). 3. Volcanic Mountains: Formed by the accumulation of volcanic lava and ash (e.g., Mt. Kilimanjaro in Africa, Mt. Fuji in Japan).

core_concepts.title: Highest Peaks of the Continents (The Seven Summits)
core_concepts.description: Asia: Mt. Everest (Nepal/China). Africa: Mt. Kilimanjaro (Tanzania). North America: Mt. Denali / formerly McKinley (Alaska, USA). South America: Mt. Aconcagua (Argentina). Europe: Mt. Elbrus (Russia). Antarctica: Vinson Massif.

core_concepts.title: The Pacific 'Ring of Fire'
core_concepts.description: This is a massive, horseshoe-shaped seismically active belt surrounding the basin of the 'Pacific Ocean'. It is characterized by frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions. Over 75% of the Earth's active volcanoes are located precisely along this ring.

core_concepts.title: Strait vs. Isthmus
core_concepts.description: Strait: A narrow body of 'water' that connects two larger bodies of water (e.g., the Palk Strait connects the Bay of Bengal to the Arabian Sea between India and Sri Lanka). Isthmus: A narrow strip of 'land' that connects two larger landmasses (e.g., the Isthmus of Panama connects North and South America).

important_entities.name: Mariana Trench
important_entities.significance: Located in the western Pacific Ocean, the Mariana Trench (specifically a spot called the 'Challenger Deep') is the deepest known point on the Earth's surface (nearly 11 kilometers deep). It is deeper than Mount Everest is tall.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often blindly assume the Himalayas are the longest mountain range because they are the highest. This is a trap. The Himalayas are the 'Highest' (containing the tallest peaks), but the 'Longest' mountain range on land is the 'Andes', which runs along the entire western coast of South America.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Ural, Rockies, Andes, Himalayas. All of these are classic examples of Young Fold Mountains formed by plate collisions.

exam_strategy_tips: Match the following questions are highly probable here: Pair Alps -> Europe; Andes -> South America; Rockies -> North America. Rote memorize these associations.
